identified_problem: D2 rated process evidence Weak on capability verification, GenAI exposure and staff workload, and Moderate on authorship assurance. No logged AI-use measure was associated with assignment marks, exam marks or the gap between them [D26], [J6], and student-kept records were often incomplete or fabricated [R45], [R72], [R27]. Submitted AI conversations made marking much slower and more subjective [S123], and marks did not respond to verbatim AI-authored code [J1].
recommended_redesign: Capture process records automatically in a university-managed workspace (AI tool, coding environment, version history) rather than relying on student-written journals [R77], [R81], [J1].
Trace each part of the submission to the captured record and treat unexplained content only as a trigger for a check (proposal) [J1], [R77].
Have staff assess the quality of AI interactions against a published rubric, weighted by the learning outcome, with moderation between markers [R17], [R91].

Triangulate the record with a short live check drawn from it, covering everyone in small cohorts and a sample plus flagged cases in large ones, and never treat a flag alone as misconduct [R81], [R77], [S457].
justification: Finding: in a computing module of 60 students, take-home scores averaged about 83.8% while viva scores averaged about 35.2%, and after repository history was triangulated with a structured viva and supervised demo the mean Learning Integrity Score rose from about 11.7 to about 45.3 [R81]. In another computing course, keystroke logs identified anomalous authorship with 87.13% accuracy but falsely flagged some honest students with heavy delete-and-rewrite styles [R77]. Interpretation: process records show what a student did with AI, not what the student understands [D26], [J6], so they add most value as the basis for a verification conversation rather than as evidence on their own.
implementation_considerations: Cohort size: manual review of logs is feasible in small cohorts [R72], [R79]. In medium cohorts, repository triangulation ran with 60 students [R81], and courses of 88 and 119 students point to the need for structured, length-limited formats [R15], [S123]. In large cohorts, manual review of every record is reported as impractical, so capture and triage must be automated [S342], [R16], [R77].

Tools and cost: only 5.3% of capstone students used the university-hosted AI tool [D14], so complete AI logs need institution-controlled tools, which links to the team's Strategy D [R16]. Keystroke capture needed a custom web editor [R77].
Privacy and policy: address privacy, consent and data handling before collecting IDE or prompt-log data [R28], [R15], [R20].

Equity: behavioural flags can wrongly flag honest students with atypical working styles [R77], treating chat logs as misconduct evidence may disadvantage multilingual students [S457], and required tools should be free to students [R15].
Staff time: budget for the viva and demonstration that make the records meaningful; no study measured staff marking time for process evidence in large computing cohorts [S123], [S342].
evidence_status_basis: R81 (computing = Y; 60 undergraduates; two-phase practitioner action research) implemented a repository with version history plus a structured viva and a supervised live demo, and reported a rise in mean Learning Integrity Score from about 11.7 to about 45.3; it used a convenience sample taught by the researcher with no control group. R09 (computing = Y; 17 first-year learners) marked students' prompting journeys and critiques, R15 (computing = Y; 88 students) gave marks for prompts, AI outputs and reflection with perception and pass data only, and R72 (computing = Y; course of typically 25-35) required interaction logs and a video, with poor documentation quality. Structured, length-limited AI-conversation formats are recommended by S123 (computing = Partial) but were not tested, and sampled review of automatically flagged logs at scale has not been evaluated; R77 is not in the tested index.
risks_and_limits: Process records cannot on their own establish understanding [D26], [J6]. Prompt histories and logs can be scripted, curated or fabricated [R17], [S457], students can transcribe AI code to avoid capture [R77], and work done in external tools is not captured [D14]. The gain in R81 comes from one module without a control group and may reflect the viva and demonstration more than the repository record. Staff time at scale is unmeasured.
